Setting time or resources aside (sense 2) and its na + Accusative purpose and dla allocation semantics are a separate meaning and receive no Phase 4 product row here; sense 2 was inspected only as a contrast boundary.

Performing the activity named by an adjacent noun (WSJP sense 2), e.g. doing the laundry. The Accusative names the activity, not a created entity. Individual robić + noun collocations are not promoted into separate governed frames beyond this one schema. Not merged with the creation sense above.

Making or creating an entity (WSJP sense 1). The Accusative names the thing created. Materials, tools, place, purpose, beneficiary, time, and manner are not complements. Not merged with the activity-performance sense below despite sharing the Accusative surface.

Comprehending communicated or represented content (WSJP sense 1): bare Accusative content, a że-clause, or an interrogative-dependent clause (how/why/what/etc., all one clause type, never separate frames). Degree, manner, language of presentation, information source, and circumstances are not complements. No clause is transferred to the person-understanding sense below.
Empathically understanding a person (WSJP sense 4), a separate meaning from comprehending content even though both surface as Accusative. No content clause attaches here.

Bringing a noun- or infinitive-denoted activity to completion (WSJP sense 1). Two alternatives: bare Accusative task/activity, or an infinitive naming the completed activity. Completion time, deadline, place, manner, and result circumstances are not complements. z + Instrumental belongs only to the separate cessation meaning below and is never added here. Nothing is inherited from kończyć.
Colloquial definitive ceasing of an activity or habit (WSJP sense 4) — a separate sense, not a variant of task completion. z + Instrumental names the activity or habit being given up for good.

A completed/bounded social meeting or contact, independently evidenced from spotykać się (Batch 05 §41). Same z + Instrumental meeting-partner schema and the same singular/reciprocal-plural participant treatment. się is part of the lexical identity. Time, place, manner, purpose, and accompanying activities are not complements.

Recurring or processual social meetings and contact. z + Instrumental names the meeting partner for a singular personal subject. A reciprocal plural personal subject (e.g. 'we meet') may occur without a separate partner phrase; this is a participant/usage restriction, not a second complementless pattern. się is part of the lexical identity, not a free complement. Frequency, time, place, manner, purpose, and accompanying activities are not complements.

Teaching a school subject (WSJP non-reflexive sense 2). The exact source schema is (KOGO) + CZEGO + GDZIE: the learner is optional, the subject Genitive is required, and the generalized GDZIE place position is verified source evidence that the locked four-type model cannot represent — it receives no complement, no preposition and no pattern, and no w, na, u or other concrete place form may be derived from it. Non-reflexive identity as above.

Teaching or instructing a learner or entity — imparting content, a skill, a proposition, procedural information or a topic (WSJP non-reflexive sense 1). The five alternatives are strict alternatives and must never be merged into one maximal frame. The Accusative position covers a person or another taught entity; in the o + Locative alternative the source restricts it to a person, which is recorded here rather than in the role. The authored identity is non-reflexive uczyć: nothing is inherited from the separate lemma uczyć się, and no example may use it.

Arranging a meeting with another person (WSJP sense 1). Two source schemas: one fully optional (a partner and an appointment/event, neither forced required), and one representing a selected venue/service position through a narrowed do + Genitive realization — do + Genitive is required only in that one product row because the row exists to represent that position, never because do is exclusive government or the only possible location form. A further source-selected time position (KIEDY) has no documented concrete realization and is intentionally not represented as any complement. A reciprocal plural personal subject ("we arranged to meet") may occur without a separate partner phrase; this is a usage fact, not a second complementless pattern. się is part of canonicalLemma, never a complement.

Reaching an agreement with another person about a term, action, or proposition (WSJP sense 2), entirely separate from arranging a meeting. Five representable content alternatives (na, o, że, żeby, interrogative-dependent), each with an optional z + Instrumental partner never split into its own pattern. A sixth source-listed alternative, co do + Genitive, is verified linguistic evidence but cannot be represented in the locked schema (which accepts only single-word prepositions); it is architecture-deferred to Phase 4C, never encoded as co or do alone, and contributes no product row here. A reciprocal plural subject may occur without a separate partner phrase, recorded as usage, not a second pattern. się is part of canonicalLemma, never a complement.

Trying not to experience, participate in, do, or contact the object. Direct Genitive is the sole authorized construction. Infinitive government was explicitly rejected by Phase 3 and is not authored; a Genitive gerund/action noun remains a noun in Genitive, not an infinitive complement.

Knowing content that can be stated as true (WSJP sense 1), with nominal, topical, propositional and interrogative-dependent content as four alternatives of one meaning. The alternatives are never cumulative. The source also selects a generalized SKĄD source-of-knowledge position: it is verified evidence but has no representable form in the locked four-type model, so it receives no complement and no pattern, and no od/z or other concrete source preposition may ever be inferred from it. A czy sentence is one surface realization of the interrogative-dependent clause, never a separate clause kind. No syntax from znać.
Imperfective return to a place previously occupied. The do and z forms are concrete realizations of selected return-goal and return-source positions, not exclusive government.

Bounded perfective return to a place previously occupied. This independently evidenced meaning uses concrete do and z realizations of selected return-goal and return-source positions, not exclusive government.

Leaving a bounded area by transport. z+Genitive realizes a selected source role, not exclusive government. Excludes destination, vehicle, route, time, and manner. No syntax is borrowed from imperfective wyjeżdżać.

Literal exit from a bounded place. z+Genitive realizes a selected source role; do+Genitive and na+Accusative realize a selected destination role. All are non-exclusive realizations. Excludes the separately evidenced ranking/result sense (na+Accusative, e.g. 'wyjść na prowadzenie'), which is not authored in this record; also excludes route, time, and manner. No syntax is borrowed from imperfective wychodzić.

A person requiring conduct or a trait. Genitive names the required content; optional od + Genitive names the person the requirement is directed at; żeby introduces a clause. The optional od participant here is restricted to a person, unlike the situation-requires meaning below. od + Genitive is directly selected by this schema, not a narrowed realization of a generalized role. There is no standalone od + Genitive construction; od only appears optionally alongside the required Genitive or żeby complement.

A situation making conduct or a condition necessary. Genitive names the required content; optional od + Genitive names the person or thing the requirement is directed at (broader than the person-only restriction above); żeby introduces a clause. Not merged with the person-requires meaning despite the shared surface forms. There is no standalone od + Genitive construction; od only appears optionally alongside the required Genitive or żeby complement.

Bounded literal grasping/taking, independently evidenced from brać. Same two alternatives: Accusative with optional Instrumental means (animate subject), and Accusative with required za + Accusative gripped part (personal subject). Destination, time, manner, and circumstance are not complements.

Fixed lexical construction wziąć udział w czymś = entry into participation, a separate WSJP fixed entry, independently evidenced from brać's. udział is required lexical material, not a replaceable object; only w + Locative is structurally encoded. A personal subject is required. Participation modifiers, event circumstances, time, and manner are not complements.

Bounded onset of an activity. Accusative names the activity as a direct object; infinitive names the action begun. Both are independently evidenced for perfective zacząć; no syntax is inherited from the metadata-only imperfective partner zaczynać.

Ordering or commissioning something for payment. Accusative names the ordered item. Dative and dla+Genitive are alternative beneficiary realizations of the same participant, not combined into one frame. u+Genitive is a documented realization of a selected provider/location role, not exclusive provider government. No syntax is borrowed from perfective zamówić.

Failing to perform an action that should have been performed. Infinitive is the sole authorized construction. The proposed żeby-clause was explicitly rejected by Phase 3 evidence and must not be authored here. No syntax is inherited from another aspect identity; this meaning is kept separate from the recall/forgetting sense above.

Losing recall of people, things, events, or information. Direct Genitive and direct Accusative both realize the remembered/forgotten object; o+Locative names a remembered topic; że clauses realize forgotten propositional content and interrogative-dependent clauses realize forgotten question content (a czy sentence is one realization of that clause type, never a separate clause kind). All are directly verified for this exact sense. Excludes the distinct failure-to-act meaning below and does not use żeby; that schema was explicitly rejected by Phase 3.

Inviting a person to an event/activity, a destination/institution, or another selected place (WSJP sense 1). Source gives KOGO + na CO | do CZEGO and separately KOGO + GDZIE: the invitee is required in both, while na + Accusative (event/activity) and do + Genitive (destination/institution) are alternative, exact concrete Składnia positions, never simultaneous slots and never described as narrowed realizations or exclusive government. The separate generalized GDZIE schema is selected source evidence that receives no product row; it stays fully unconcretized — no w, u, na + Locative, or other place form may ever be derived from it.

Lexical-reflexive consent to a proposal or action (WSJP sense 1); się is part of the canonical lemma identity, never a complement. Source gives na KOGO/CO, żeby ZDANIE, infinitive, and direct speech: four alternative content schemas, none parenthesised, none carrying a partner position. No z + Instrumental partner belongs here; that relation is exclusive to opinion-agreement. Kept strictly separate from opinion/interpersonal agreement and from matching/correspondence, which is excluded entirely.
